content:
incident-bot: [ALERT] hosted-api.p95 latency > 2s and request_queue depth > 12k for the past 3m in us-west-2. Autoscaler reports repeated scale_limit_reached. Paging @op-oncall :rotating_light:
op-oncall: on it. grabbing logs + checking autoscaler events. any customer-facing errors?
maya: customers reporting intermittent 504s from the hosted API, some 429s. looking at per-route metrics — text-generation v2 routes are the worst. p95 ~ 2.6s, p99 ~ 7.8s on the dash.
jonathan: confirming GPU pool us-west-2-g1 is saturated. queue_growth_rate = 40r/s, processed_rate = 12r/s. autoscaler kept trying to add pods but hit quota
ops-bot: autoscaler event stream:
```
2026-03-15T02:08:42Z scale_attempt(pool=us-west-2-g1, requested=6, current=24)
2026-03-15T02:08:44Z error=scale_limit_reached(reason=project_quota)
2026-03-15T02:09:10Z scale_attempt(pool=us-west-2-g1, requested=6, current=24)
2026-03-15T02:09:13Z error=scale_limit_reached(reason=project_quota)
```
op-oncall: looks like quota/limits preventing more GPUs. can we route to dedicated fallback pools or use lower-memory quantized variant?
sara: we have a warm quantized variant ql-3-small that fits current nodes. but it has slightly lower quality. question: do we prefer to maintain availability for all customers or keep quality for a subset?
derek: ops suggestion — emergency routing policy: route non-SLA traffic to ql-3-small, route SLA customers to reserved-dedicated-1. we can also enable shedding of low-priority routes.
maya: customer impact list — some mid-market PLG customers are seeing timeouts in the webhooks that call our textgen route. one payment partner reported 504s for webhook retries. i'll open a support ticket and notify CS.
jonathan: I'm going to open the emergency routing flag now. command: 
```
redwoodctl route update --route /v1/generate --policy emergency-fallback --variants ql-3-small:0.8,redwood-1:0.2
```
jonathan: applied, rolling changes. watching request flow.
ops-bot: route change accepted. new routing weight: ql-3-small 80%, redwood-1 20%.
op-oncall: traffic shifted. processed_rate increased to 28r/s, queue depth down to 7.2k within 90s. p95 trending down to 1.4s. p99 still ~4.5s.
sara: enabling prefix cache warm for ql-3-small to avoid cold kv cache storms. running cache-warm job for top 500 prefixes.
derek: also enabling temporary request-shed for free-tier endpoints. command:
```
redwoodctl quota adjust --group free-tier --rate 0.6
```
maya: support update: CS notified customers A12, Bcorp, and green-field about degraded performance and mitigation steps. sent status note and ETA ~30-45m.
jonathan: attempted manual quota bump request to cloud provider; support says we'll get capacity in ~2-3 hours if approved. not helpful for immediate mitigation.
op-oncall: we should also open a fallback region for overflow (us-east-1). risk is data residency for some customers. any objections?
sara: ok for non-residency customers. creating routing policy to prefer us-west-2, overflow to us-east-1 for non-sensitive traffic.
ops-bot: policy change queued. NOTE: some pods in us-east-1 will need model pull; estimated cold fetch time ~ 2m per node, but parallelizable.
derek: monitoring customer error rates — overall 504s down 70% since routing changes. user-visible latency for premium customers is stable. free-tier still sees some hitches until cache warms.
maya: putting a public status update draft in #incidents-status for review:
```
We are currently experiencing increased latency and timeouts on the hosted API due to GPU capacity limitations triggered by an unexpected traffic surge. We have activated fallback routing to lower-memory quantized model variants and shifted non-SLA traffic to alternate regions. Premium customers are being served from reserved capacity. Mitigation in progress; estimated restoration within 30-60 minutes.
```
jonathan: deployment note — we saw several backend connection resets from inference runtime: `kv_cache_oom` spikes concurrent with queue bursts. investigating whether cache eviction policy contributed.
sara: cache eviction was aggressive at the time of surge because KV usage spiked from long-context requests. added a temporary increase to kv-cache-size on the ql-3-small nodes. command:
```
infractl node update --pool us-west-2-g1 --kv-cache-size 48GB
```
ops-bot: node update in progress. expected effect within 60s per node as sidecar restarts.
op-oncall: we need to start formal incident doc. I'll collect timeline, impact, and steps taken. assigning severity: Sev2 (partial outage impacting non-trivial customer subset).
derek: do we need to trigger exec-level notification? recommend not yet; keep exec informed via summary.
maya: handoff note — my shift ends in 30m. @jonathan will take next on-call. I'll post a thorough rundown and handoff checklist in 15m.
jonathan: acknowledged. I'll keep monitoring for at least 1h post-restoration.
ops-bot: metric snapshot (02:12 — after routing): queue_depth=7200, processed_rate=30r/s, error_rate_504=0.9%, p95=1.2s, p99=3.7s.
op-oncall: all mitigation actions so far: 1) emergency routing to ql-3-small, 2) free-tier shedding, 3) overflow to us-east-1 for non-residency traffic, 4) kv-cache-size bump. current status: partial mitigation succeeded, but backend quota still blocking autoscaler full recovery.
sara: next steps: continue cache warm job, monitor dedicated pool for premium migrations, log all autoscaler error events for postmortem.
maya: support posting sent. CS will escalate any urgent paid-customer cases.
jonathan: leaving a quick checklist for handoff:
- confirm queue_depth trending down for 15m
- ensure cache_warm job finished
- watch for new scale_limit_reached events
- keep support thread open and update customers every 30m
- if p99 > 5s again, re-enable higher fallback weighting to ql-3-small

maya: handing off to @jonathan. tagging pager: @op-oncall if it re-escalates. :white_check_mark:
jonathan: taking handoff. I'll post a follow-up thread when incident is declared resolved.
ops-bot: incident thread created: https://redwood/status/incident/2032104567
